analysis.openHint: Sun hours, irradiation, EN 17037 and the site's climate
analysis.title: Solar & climate analysis
analysis.noLocation: Set the site's location in the sun study first: everything here depends on where the building is.

climate.title: Site climate
climate.consent: Load observed weather for this place from Open-Meteo (ERA5): 10 years of daily normals and 5 years of hourly direct and diffuse radiation. Only the coordinates, rounded to ~1 km, are sent.
climate.error: The climate could not be loaded: {{message}}

period.title: Period
period.needsClimate: Load the climate to know the seasons

en.title: EN 17037 sunlight exposure
en.summary: {{pass}} of {{total}} windows reach the minimum (1.5 h)
en.note: Hours of direct sun on each window's outer face on 21 March. A screening: the standard measures at a reference point inside the room, with a minimum sun altitude set nationally.

gain.title: Overheating and winter gain
gain.noRisk: No glazing above 2 kWh/m²·day in the hot season.
gain.note: Average daily irradiation per m² of glazing. Above ~3.5 kWh/m²·day in summer a window needs shading; above ~2.5 in winter it is real free heating. Indicative bands, not a thermal simulation.

analysis.disclaimer: Sun from the NOAA/SPA algorithm; sky from ERA5 measurements when loaded (else a clear sky scaled by measured clearness); Hay–Davies diffuse weighted by the sky each point really sees. For design decisions — not an energy certificate.

metricHint.sunHours: Hours the sun is visible from each point (clear sky) — what EN 17037 counts
metricHint.probableSun: Hours of sun to expect, with the site's measured chance of sunshine at each hour
metricHint.irradiation: Solar energy received: beam + diffuse sky + light reflected by the ground
metricHint.skyView: Share of the sky a point sees, cosine-weighted (100 % = a roof under an open sky). Drives daylight and night cooling

sky.label: Sky
sky.fallback: Not loaded yet — using: {{model}}. Load the climate for the measured sky.

analysis.exportGridHint: Every sensor with its position, normal and all the metrics (CSV)

timelapse.title: Day timelapse
timelapse.export: Export the day as a video

almanac.title: Almanac & sun path
almanac.diagram: Sun-path diagram: the year's envelope, today's arc and the sun and moon now
almanac.shadowHint: Length of the shadow a 10 m vertical object casts on flat ground right now
almanac.source: Sun: NOAA/Meeus algorithm with refraction (±0.01°). Moon: suncalc. Times in the site's zone ({{offset}}).

probe.title: Shading diagram of a point
probe.picking: Click the model or the site… (Esc)
probe.nothing: Nothing there to measure — click the model, the city or the ground.
probe.hint: Click a window, a terrace, a spot of the plot: see what blocks its sky over the year's sun paths, and its sun hour by hour, month by month.
probe.diagram: Shading diagram: the point's obstructions over the sun paths of the 21st of each month
probe.year: Sun per day, year (vs. open sky)
probe.table: Sun on the 21st, hour by hour (share of each hour)

shading.title: Solar protections
shading.suggestHint: Deep enough to shade the window fully at summer-solstice noon, shallow enough to let the winter sun in
shading.hint: Choose the façades and the devices; they are drawn on every window facing there. Measuring runs the hot season, the cold season and the EN 17037 day on those windows, with and without them.
shading.noWindows: The model has no windows to shade
shading.stale: The design changed — measure again to update.
shading.note: Same windows, same sky, same engine: the only difference is the devices. Averages weighted by glazed area.

pv.title: Solar panels
pv.working: Following the sun over the year…
pv.noRoof: The model has no roof surfaces facing up
pv.hint: A year on the roofs at the panels' own angle (tilted rows on flat roofs, flush on pitches), with every shadow from the model, the city and the terrain. Usable: at least the chosen share of the roof's best spot.
pv.note: Rows on flat roofs spaced so the winter noon sun clears them. Yield = irradiation on the modules × efficiency × performance ratio (inverter, temperature, soiling, wiring). A pre-design estimate — not an installer's quote.
pv.clearSky: Clear sky: without the measured climate the yield comes out 10–20 % high. Load the climate above to use the real sky (ERA5).

report.title: Solar study
report.empty: Compute something first (an analysis, a check, a point, protections, panels, daylight or a comparison): the report gathers what has been computed.
report.sunIntro: Where the sun crosses this site's sky through the year, drawn to true north. Each curve is the 21st of a month; the dotted lines are the hours.
report.sunLegend: Red: June · grey: March/September · blue: December. Centre = zenith, rim = horizon.
report.heatmapIntro: {{metric}} over {{period}}, measured on the model with every shadow — its own, the city's and the terrain's.
report.runMeta: {{instants}} sun positions standing for {{raw}} instants · {{sensors}} sensors · sky: {{sky}} · ground albedo {{albedo}}
report.probeIntro: What blocks the sky from the point ({{x}}, {{y}}, {{z}}) — grey — over the year's sun paths, and the sun it gets hour by hour.
report.shadingIntro: {{devices}} on the {{facades}} façades. The same windows, sky and engine measured with and without them.

sun.title: Sun position
sun.body: NOAA / Meeus solar position algorithm with atmospheric refraction corrected for the site's pressure; within 0.02° of NREL's SPA reference. Times in the site's own time zone.

sky.title: Sky
sky.body: Measured: ERA5 reanalysis (Copernicus / ECMWF) via Open-Meteo — 5 years of hourly direct, diffuse and global radiation and sunshine, and 10 years of daily climate. Without it: Ineichen–Perez clear sky, split by Erbs from the measured monthly clearness.

surface.title: On each surface
surface.body: Hay–Davies: beam and circumsolar diffuse are shadowed with the sun; the isotropic sky is weighted by each point's cosine-weighted sky view; ground reflection with the chosen albedo.

engine.title: Shadows
engine.body: Thousands of sensors placed on the IFC's own windows, walls, roofs and site. For every sun position the GPU renders a shadow map of everything that can block it — the model, the surrounding OSM buildings and the terrain — and tests each sensor. Seasons and years walk every day, binned into small patches of sky.

checks.title: Checks
checks.body: EN 17037 sunlight exposure: hours of direct sun on 21 March above a minimum altitude (1.5 / 3 / 4 h). Solar gain on glazing: indicative bands, not a thermal simulation. Photovoltaics: irradiation on the module plane × efficiency × performance ratio.

limits.title: Limits
limits.body: A design-stage study to compare options and size decisions. It is not an energy certificate, a thermal simulation or an installer's quote; EN 17037 is screened at the window's outer face, not at the room's reference point.

geometry.title: Geometry
geometry.body: Every element at full detail for every pass, whatever the camera sees, and no clipping plane (section box, plan cut) reaches a measurement. Curtain-wall plates are told apart by name, description and type: opaque spandrels count as façade, not glass. Rooms are their IfcSpace volumes, footprints included.

daylight.title: Daylight in the rooms
daylight.body: Average daylight factor (BRE / CIBSE LG10) with θ from each window's measured sky view; BRE limiting depth. Point by point: a grid on the working plane (0.85 m, 0.5 m off the walls), the CIE overcast sky seen from each point through the glass (400 directions, GPU) plus BRE split-flux inter-reflections; EN 17037 targets from the site's median diffuse illuminance.

annual.title: Daylight over the year
annual.body: Daylight coefficients over the 145 Tregenza sky patches, measured once per point on the GPU; 12 × 24 typical hours of the site's sky, diffuse with the CIE overcast shape (120 lm/W), the sun in its patch (100 lm/W). EN 17037 by hourly illuminance, sDA300/50 % and ASE1000,250 h as IES LM-83 / LEED v4, without blinds.

report.compareIntro: “{{b}}” ({{pb}}) against “{{a}}” ({{pa}}), {{metric}}, point by point on the model. Red: better, blue: worse.
report.daylightIntro: Average daylight factor of every room from its windows and the sky they see (sky: {{sky}}). Glass transmittance {{T}} %, room reflectance {{R}} %.
report.summaryIntro: Every check computed for this model, one verdict each. The pages that follow give the detail and the method.

sum.enSunNote: Windows with ≥ 1.5 h of sun on 21 March above {{alt}}°, at their outer face.
sum.daylight: Daylight provision, EN 17037 (rooms, point by point)
sum.daylightNote: Target over ≥ 50 % of each room and the minimum over ≥ 95 %, CIE overcast sky.
sum.daylightNarrow: {{n}} rooms pass only with reflected light (simplified BRE): a narrow pass.
sum.daylightAvgNote: BRE average daylight factor against the EN 17037 target — run the point-by-point map for the standard's own test.
sum.leed: Daylight over the year, LEED v4 (sDA ≥ 55 %, ASE ≤ 10 %)
sum.leedNote: Climate-based, every typical hour of the year.
sum.leedGlare: {{n}} rooms get too much direct sun (ASE > 10 %): glare and overheating risk.
sum.deep: Rooms deeper than the BRE limiting depth
sum.deepNote: Their back half stays dim whatever the window.
sum.overheatNote: Windows above 3.5 kWh/m²·day in the hot season need shading.
sum.point: Sun at the studied point (yearly mean per day)
sum.pointNote: {{en}} h on 21 March (EN 17037 at that point).
sum.compareNote: {{metric}} — better on {{better}} of the windows, worse on {{worse}}.
sum.onlyMaps: Only maps were computed: run the checks for verdicts.
sum.noClimate: The site's measured climate was not loaded: results use a clear sky (sunnier than reality). Load it for ERA5-based figures.
sum.optNote: ASE from {{from}} % unprotected; keeps a DA300 of {{da}} %.

report.annualIntro: Climate-based daylight: every typical hour of the year with this site's sky and sun, through the glass, on each room's working plane.
report.annualMap: Daylight autonomy (DA300) — the floor that does worst
report.annualDelta: In brackets: change in percentage points against the previous annual run (for example, without protections).
report.blindsOn: sDA with IES LM-83 operable blinds (down when > 2 % of the room gets > 1000 lx of direct sun; closed they pass 20 % of the diffuse). ASE without blinds. “Blinds”: share of the occupied hours with them down.
report.blindsOff: Computed without blinds: this sDA is not LEED's (LM-83 requires operable blinds).
report.optIntro: {{n}} standard protections tried on the {{list}} façades, each with the full annual daylight method (blinds as set), ranked by LEED's reading: ASE ≤ 10 % first, then the most daylight.
report.optNote: In brackets: ASE change against no protection, in points. Coarser grid than the main annual run (~2 000 points): for ranking designs; run the year again with the chosen one for the final figures.

compare.title: Compare design variants
compare.hint: Save the result on screen as a variant, change the design (protections, another IFC version, the sky) and run again: then compare the two point by point on the model.
compare.moreIsBetter: More irradiation is better (panels, winter gain)
compare.periodMismatch: Careful: the variant measured {{a}}, the current result {{b}}.
compare.legend: Change from “{{a}}” to the current result — {{metric}}
compare.paired: {{pct}} % of the current surfaces have a partner in the variant (new or moved surfaces show grey).

daylight.title: Daylight in the rooms
daylight.noSpaces: The model has no rooms (IfcSpace): daylight is measured per room.
daylight.hint: For every IfcSpace: its windows, the sky they really see (the city and the building included), the average daylight factor (BRE) and the EN 17037 daylight level it reaches.
daylight.summary: {{ok}} of {{lit}} rooms with windows reach the minimum ({{rooms}} rooms in all)
daylight.targets: EN 17037 targets here: {{min}} % (300 lx) · {{med}} % (500 lx) · {{high}} % (750 lx) — median outdoor diffuse light {{lux}} lx
daylight.rowHint: Visible sky θ {{theta}}° · depth {{depth}} m (limit {{limit}} m)
daylight.tooDeep: Deeper than the BRE limiting depth: the back of the room will look dark
daylight.deepNote: {{n}} rooms are deeper than the BRE limiting depth (L/W + L/H ≤ 2/(1−Rb)): their back half stays dim whatever the window.
daylight.note: Average daylight factor (BRE / CIBSE LG10) with θ from each window's measured sky view; rooms as their IfcSpace boxes. EN 17037 by the daylight-factor method on the room average — a screening, the standard asks for the target over half of the room's area.
daylight.gridHint: A grid on each room's working plane (0.85 m, 0.5 m off the walls): the CIE overcast sky each point sees through the glass, plus inter-reflections. EN 17037 asks for the target over 50 % of the plane and the minimum over 95 %.
daylight.gridStale: Transmittance or reflectance changed — map again to update the points.
daylight.noGrid: No room is big enough for a grid 0.5 m off its walls.
daylight.gridSummary: Point by point: {{ok}} of {{lit}} rooms meet EN 17037 ({{points}} points every {{spacing}} m)
daylight.shareHint: Share of the room's plane at or above the 300 lx target (EN 17037 asks 50 %)
daylight.onReflections: {{n}} rooms only pass thanks to reflected light (the simplified BRE formula, uniform over the room): on the sky their points see they would not. Treat it as a narrow pass.
daylight.annualHint: Climate-based: every typical hour of the year (12 months × 24 h) with the site's sky, the sun included. EN 17037 by hourly illuminance, sDA300/50 % and ASE1000,250 h (LEED v4 / IES LM-83).
daylight.annualClearSky: No measured sky: a clear sky × the monthly clearness stands in. Load the climate for the ERA5 hours — annual results depend on them.
daylight.annualSummary: {{ok}} of {{n}} rooms meet EN 17037 by the hour · {{leed}} meet LEED (sDA ≥ 55 %, ASE ≤ 10 %) — {{points}} points every {{spacing}} m
daylight.daHint: Daylight autonomy: mean share of daylight hours at ≥ 300 lx
daylight.sdaHint: sDA300/50 %: share of the room at ≥ 300 lx for half the occupied hours (08–18 h); LEED asks ≥ 55 %
daylight.aseHint: ASE1000,250 h: share of the room with > 1000 lx of direct sun for > 250 occupied hours; LEED asks ≤ 10 % (glare, overheating)
daylight.annualNote: Daylight coefficients over the 145 Tregenza patches and a second pass at each hour's actual sun position; diffuse with the CIE overcast shape scaled to the hour's diffuse (120 lm/W), direct sun 100 lm/W, BRE reflections of the diffuse only (reflected sunlight is not counted: conservative). No blinds, 12 typical days. A design-stage screening, not a Radiance simulation.
daylight.annualVsPrev: Change against the run at {{at}} (percentage points)
daylight.blindsHint: Each hour, in each room, they come down when over 2 % of its points get more than 1000 lx of direct sun: no sun, 20 % of the diffuse. This is how LEED computes sDA; ASE is always measured without them.
daylight.blindHoursHint: Share of the occupied hours with the blinds down: a lot means glare and the lights on

optimizer.title: Find the protection
optimizer.hint: Tries {{n}} designs (none, overhangs, fins, louvres) on the sun-facing façades, each measured over the year, and ranks them: ASE ≤ 10 % first, then the most daylight. Click one to put it on the model.
optimizer.facades: On the {{list}} façades. ● applied; click a row to apply it.
optimizer.apply: Put this design on the model
optimizer.found: The first design brings ASE to the LEED limit (≤ 10 %) and keeps the most daylight among those that do.
optimizer.notFound: No design here reaches ASE ≤ 10 %: the first one comes closest. Deeper or denser screening, or less glass, is needed.
